newsitem.title: UK: Prodi underlines Italy's EMU commitment - FT.
newsitem.headline: Prodi underlines Italy's EMU commitment - FT.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi is confident implementation of last February's tough budget will make it impossible for the nation to be left out of European economic and monetary union (EMU), the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
"The budget is remarkably tough. If we do all this, it will be impossible to leave Italy out of monetary union," Prodi told the newspaper in an interview.
Prodi, who took office in May as the head of Italy's first centre-left administration, said the country has begun to make serious adjustments.
He said Rome was aiming to bring its deficit as a proportion of GDP down to three percent, from 4.5 percent, to meet the Maastricht criteria for membership of the EMU.
Prodi used to feel it would not be a "tragedy" if Italy was late in meeting the criteria. However, he now felt the country must not be left out, the paper said.

"The change occurred after the summer when I saw that other countries were making a serious effort to address their budget deficits...I realised Italy, too, could not miss out on this appointment with Europe," Prodi said.
And he believed Britain would not want to miss out either.
"I have always believed the City of London would not miss the opportunities created by monetary union...When it comes to the time, the UK will think twice before missing the boat," Prodi told the FT.
He also said in the interview that spending on health and public administration in Italy was not high by European standards, and the nation had moved to curb pensions abuses.
But a comprehensive reassessment of Italy's pensions system is made impossible by a 1995 agreement between the unions and the former government of Lamberto Dini.

"The previous government gave an undertaking that any further structural changes in pensions could not be done until January 1998. We have to respect that," Prodi said, adding that there is a need for consensus on social issues.
